{{< include mds/_subfiles/algebra/_def-range-of-variable.qmd >}}

For example,
if $x$ is the number of heads in two tosses of a coin,
then $\rangef{x} = \cb{0, 1, 2}$.
A [random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-random-variable) $X$
(defined in the Morrison Lab's probability notes)
is a [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function),
and the set of values $X$ can take, $\rangef{X}$,
is the [image](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-image) of $X$.
These notes use "range" only for variables:
for a function, "range" can mean either the image or the codomain
([Range](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-range)).
In statistics, "the range" of a dataset can also mean
its largest value minus its smallest value;
$\rangef{x}$ is a set, not that difference.

{{< slidebreak >}}

@tbl-notational-shorthands lists shorthands you may encounter in other sources,
the full form each one abbreviates,
and the part each one leaves out.
In the table,
$\dsn{x}$ and $\dsn{a}$ are $n$ numbers,
$b_{ij}$ is the entry in row $i$ and column $j$ of an $m \times n$ array,
$k$ is an integer with $1 \le k \le n$,
$f$ is a [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function)
from $\reals$ to $\reals$,
and, in the first row, $\rangef{x}$ is a finite set.

| Shorthand | Full form | Part left out |
|:----------|:----------|:--------------|
| $\sum_{x} f(x)$ | $\sum_{x \in \rangef{x}} f(x)$ | the set the sum runs over ([sum over a finite set](algebra.qmd#def-sum-over-set)) |
| $\sum_{i} x_i$ | $\sumin x_i$ | the lower and upper limits of the index ([summation notation](algebra.qmd#def-summation)) |
| $\sum x_i$ | $\sumin x_i$ | the index and its lower and upper limits |
| $\prod_{i} x_i$ | $\prodin x_i$ | the lower and upper limits of the index |
| $\prod x_i$ | $\prodin x_i$ | the index and its lower and upper limits |
| $\sum_{i, j} b_{ij}$ | $\sumto{i}{m} \sumjn b_{ij}$ | the limits of both indices |
| $\sum_{i \neq k} a_i$ | $\sum_{i \in \cb{1, \ldots, n} \setminus \cb{k}} a_i$ | the set $\cb{1, \ldots, n}$ of indices that $k$ is removed from |
| $\int f(x)\,dx$, used for a number | $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx$ | the limits of integration |
| $\int f$ | $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx$ | the limits, the variable of integration, and the differential $dx$ |
| $x_{1:n}$ | $(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n)$ | the explicit list of entries |
| "the function $x^2$" | "the function $f : \reals \to \reals$ with $f(x) = x^2$" | the function's name, domain, and codomain |
